calls.head: St. Louis gets to the dangerous areas
calls.body: St. Louis ranks 6th of 32 for shot quality (one expected goal for every 15.0 unblocked shots); San Jose ranks 23rd for keeping shots to the outside.
calls.call: St. Louis needs no more than its usual 15.0 unblocked shots per expected goal.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: St. Louis needed 9.9 unblocked shots per expected goal, against its usual 15.0.

calls.head: A low-event night is likely
calls.body: San Jose’s games average only 78.5 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined (29th of 32 for pace); St. Louis’s average 78.5 (28th).
calls.call: The game runs at fewer than the two teams’ usual 78.5 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 3 and 3 games this season
calls.happened: The game ran at 76.7 unblocked shots per 60 at 5-on-5, both teams combined, against the two teams’ usual 78.5 and a league average of 81.7.

STL.head: We had this close to even (60% for St. Louis), and it went San Jose’s way.

SJS.head: We had this close to even (40% for San Jose), and San Jose came through.

surprises.head: St. Louis got to the dangerous areas
surprises.body: St. Louis needed 9.9 unblocked shots per expected goal at 5-on-5, against its usual 15.0 and a league average of 15.8. Over the last three seasons, a team strayed this far about once every 80 games.

surprises.head: San Jose won against the run of play
surprises.body: Replaying this game’s chances, St. Louis comes out ahead 73 times in 100. San Jose won anyway.
